summary: You live alone on the 3rd floor and use a powered wheelchair. Your lift needs electricity, and you haven’t arranged help yet. Start by agreeing an accessible way to leave, a backup-power plan, and a cool place you can reach.

gaps.title: No agreed way to leave without the lift
gaps.why: You live alone on the 3rd floor. A power cut could stop the lift.
gaps.fix: Talk with your building manager and a trusted person about an accessible evacuation plan. Confirm who can help and a backup contact.

gaps.title: Your chair depends on power
gaps.why: Your powered wheelchair needs charging, but no backup plan is described.
gaps.fix: Ask your chair supplier about safe backup power and charging options. Write down your equipment needs and key contacts.

gaps.title: A cool, accessible place is not identified
gaps.why: Heat and a power cut could make staying home difficult.
gaps.fix: Find an accessible cool place and check transport options in advance. Ask NYC services about current cooling-centre availability.

checklist.step: Save official alert links and emergency contacts
Agree an accessible evacuation and backup-power plan
Check official instructions and contact your support person
Charge your chair and phone; gather essential supplies
Follow local instructions and use your agreed support plan
In immediate danger, call 911 and explain your access needs

comparison.personalised: Agree how to leave your 3rd-floor home if the lift loses power. Include a trusted helper and backup contact.
Include your chair’s charging needs, equipment information, medicines and support contacts in your plan.
Identify a cool place you can enter with your wheelchair, and check how you would get there without the lift.
